question.problem: What is the remainder when $3{x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}+5{x}^{2}-1$ is divided by $3{x}^{2}+2x-1?$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the $x$ term. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing term with a coefficient of zero, as follows:

$$
3{x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}+5{x}^{2}-1=3{x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}+5{x}^{2}+0x-1
$$

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,{x}^{2}+2 \\  & 3{x}^{2}+2x-1\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,3{x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}+5{x}^{2}+0x-1\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,{\,\,3{x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\text{ }6{x}^{2}+0x-1 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{6{x}^{2}+4x-2}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,-\,4x+1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

- the quotient is ${x}^{2}+2,$ and

- the remainder is $-4x+1.$
